subject: Growth will require a mobile number at signup starting Friday to cut fake workspaces. Last month 12% of new workspaces failed a domain check. A three-day optional-phone test on 20% of signups dropped fake workspaces by half and cut completed signups by 18%.
context: Sales says three late-stage prospects complained that phone-required signup felt like a consumer app. The phone field can ship behind a flag. Marketing's lead-quality bonus uses workspace count.

subject: Infrastructure will stand up an EU region before 1 March because two prospects in procurement require data residency. Build cost is about $40k and $6k a month after. Neither prospect has signed. The sales cycle for each is estimated at four months.
context: A partner offers EU hosting under the company's brand for $2k a month with a 30-day exit. Security review of the partner would take about two weeks. The board asked for a residency plan by end of quarter.

subject: Will the board chair, Elias, approve a $400k founder secondary in the Series A? He has said secondaries are allowed only when the round is oversubscribed by at least 1.5x, the company keeps twelve months of runway after the round, and no more than 10% of the round is secondary.
context: The round is currently at 1.1x soft circle. Post-round runway at the planned raise is fourteen months. The secondary would be 8% of the round. Elias decides with the board on Friday.

subject: Product will bundle the $30-per-month analytics add-on into every team plan at no extra charge starting 1 January, to reduce plan-choice friction. About 18% of team plans pay for the add-on today, worth roughly $4k MRR.
context: Competitors include basic analytics in the base plan. Turning the add-on into a default can ship as a price-page change without migrating data. Finance asked whether a $2 seat increase should land at the same time and got no answer.

subject: The company will pay a former contractor $35k to assign IP on a billing module they wrote eighteen months ago, after the contractor emailed claiming ownership. Counsel says a court fight would cost more than $35k in fees alone. The module is in production for every paying customer.
context: The original agreement had an IP assignment clause the contractor says they never signed. The countersigned PDF is missing page two. Shipping a rewrite would take about six weeks for one engineer.

subject: Will the CEO, Marta, greenlight opening a Canada entity this quarter? She has said she will only approve a new country when annual revenue from that country already exceeds $200k, legal has a named counsel on retainer, and the first hire is a contractor for at most six months.
context: Canadian revenue last year was $168k, all through a reseller. Legal has a shortlist of two firms and has not signed either. The proposed first hire is a full-time country manager at $140k. Marta reviews on Wednesday.

subject: Will the CISO, Dana, allow connecting the new analytics vendor to production event data? Dana has said a new vendor gets production access only with a signed DPA, a SOC 2 Type II less than twelve months old, and a one-week shadowed read on a redacted copy first.
context: The vendor's SOC 2 is fourteen months old and renewal is in progress. The DPA is drafted. No shadowed read has been scheduled. Dana's review is Tuesday.

subject: Customer success will cut onboarding from three live calls to one live call plus a checklist, starting with all new accounts next Monday. Median time-to-first-value is twelve days. Accounts that skipped the second call historically churned 1.4x more in ninety days.
context: CS capacity is tight: each CSM carries 45 accounts. A self-serve checklist already exists and is used by 30% of new accounts. The change can be limited to plans under $500 a month.

subject: Will the customer-success lead, Rina, approve expanding the pilot at Cobalt from 40 to 200 seats next month? She has said expansions go through only when weekly active use is above 60%, open severity-1 tickets are zero for two weeks, and the customer names a go-live owner.
context: Weekly active use is 47%. There has been one severity-1 ticket in the last two weeks, now closed. Cobalt named a go-live owner yesterday. Rina decides Thursday.

subject: Support will issue a full annual refund to a loud customer on Twitter who is 10 months into a 12-month term, against a written policy of no refunds after 30 days. The contract value is $6,400. The thread has 2,400 likes and names the company.
context: Finance has denied three similar asks this year. The product bug the customer cites was fixed six weeks ago. A partial refund of two months was floated privately and not yet offered.

subject: Will the head of sales, Owen, accept a $2.4m annual quota for next year? He has said he signs a quota only when it is at most 1.3x the trailing twelve-month closed-won, the average cycle used in the model matches the last two quarters, and ramps for two open AE seats are written in.
context: Trailing closed-won is $1.6m. The model uses a 35-day cycle; the last two quarters averaged 52 days. The two AE seats are empty and have no ramp schedule. Owen replies on Monday.

subject: The founder will retain a fractional CFO at $8k a month for six months to prepare Series A materials, instead of promoting the current bookkeeper or hiring a full-time finance lead at $180k. The bookkeeper has closed the books on time for fourteen months.
context: Investors in the last process asked for cohort gross margin the bookkeeper could not produce without help. Cash runway is nine months. No term sheet is in hand.

subject: The partnership lead will shut down the partner portal on 1 December. It has 38 registered partners, 4 of whom brought a closed deal in the last year, totaling $72k ARR. Hosting and maintenance are about $1,200 a month plus a quarter-engineer.
context: One of the four active partners is in a verbal for a $40k deal that uses portal lead forms. A static landing page with a shared inbox was proposed as a replacement and not built.

subject: Sales will require every account executive to run two public product demos a week, starting next week, to fill top-of-funnel. Demo attendance last month averaged seven people, and two of the last eight demos produced a pipeline opportunity.
context: AEs already have 60% of calendar in live deals. Marketing offered to staff demos with a solutions engineer instead. The CRM does not yet attribute demo attendance to opportunities cleanly.

subject: Growth will sell 200 lifetime licenses at $499 this month through a deal site to raise cash. Lifetime means all future team features for one workspace. Current annual team plan is $288 a year. Cash in bank covers five months of runway.
context: A similar lifetime offer two years ago still supports 140 workspaces that cost about $1,100 a month in aggregate infra and support. Finance has not modeled support load for 200 more.

subject: The founder will sign a 24-month lease on a 10-person Austin office at $9,200 a month, starting 1 February, because three hires asked for a place to meet and a competitor opened nearby. Remote stipends today are $200 a month per person.
context: Headcount is 16, all remote across four time zones. Only two of the three hires who asked live within an hour of Austin. Breaking the lease in year one costs six months of rent.

subject: Product will publish a dated public roadmap for the next two quarters on the marketing site this week, naming six features with target months. Sales has been losing deals when buyers ask what is coming. Two of the six features are still only one-page briefs.
context: A prior public roadmap slipped three of four dates and is still cited by one prospect. An undated themes page was drafted as an alternative. Legal has not reviewed the dated version.

subject: Services will raise the implementation fee from $2,500 to $6,000 for new deals starting next Monday, citing that every implementation overruns by at least ten hours. Win rate on deals that mention implementation has been 55% for two quarters.
context: Two open proposals still quote $2,500. Competitors charge $0 to $4,000. Finance wants the higher fee to stop discounting professional services into negative margin.

subject: Support will replace the shared macro library with a new AI-drafted reply tool for all agents on Monday, with no cohort flag. Average handle time is 9 minutes. A private beta with three agents cut handle time to 7 minutes on easy tickets and raised reopen rate from 4% to 9%.
context: The macros cover refunds, shipping delays, and password resets. Compliance requires a human send on refunds over $200. The AI tool can be toggled off per queue in under a minute.

subject: The founder will replace the weekly all-hands with a recorded monthly update and a written notes doc, citing that average attendance fell to 55% and the meeting takes forty minutes for twenty people. Two new hires said all-hands was how they learned priorities.
context: There is no other company-wide forum. The recorded update would still be optional to watch. Eng and GTM already run their own weekly huddles.

subject: Platform will cut the primary database over to a new provider in one maintenance window on Saturday night, moving 1.2 TB with a planned 40-minute read-only period. The last similar move at another team took 3 hours. There is a tested rollback that restores the old primary from a snapshot taken at cutover start.
context: A dual-write week was priced at two engineer-weeks and rejected to save calendar time. P95 write latency on the current primary has been fine for six months. On-call is two engineers.

subject: Marketing will buy a $28k eight-week flight on a founder podcast with an estimated 40k downloads per episode, aiming for 200 trial starts. Last quarter's comparable newsletter sponsorship produced 31 trials at $6k. Tracking links are ready.
context: The podcast has not shared audience overlap with the company's ICP beyond a one-line description. Payment is due up front and is non-refundable after the first episode airs. A smaller two-episode test was offered at $8k.

subject: Product will remove the legacy CSV importer on 15 January and tell the 62 accounts that still used it last month to switch to the API. Keeping the importer costs about half an engineer of maintenance each quarter. Two of the 62 accounts are in renewal conversations this month.
context: The API covers every CSV field except a deprecated tags column used by nine accounts. A one-click migration wizard was scoped at one week and not scheduled. Support wrote the sunset email.

subject: Engineering will move on-call from the current pager tool to a cheaper one at $12 per user per month, saving about $9k a year, with a one-weekend cutover and no overlap week. The current tool's last missed page was eight months ago.
context: The cheaper tool lacks the SMS fallback the hospital customer requires in the MSA. A webhook-to-SMS bridge was sketched at two days of work. On-call is nine engineers.

subject: People ops will send all eleven managers to a three-day offsite training at $2,200 per person plus travel, in February, after two skip-level complaints about inconsistent feedback. A two-hour virtual course from the same vendor is $180 per person.
context: Engagement survey scores on 'manager feedback' fell from 72 to 61 in six months. Three managers are new to people leadership. The budget still has $40k under learning and development.
